Chapter 4: The Importance of Individuality and Selfhood in Attraction
Have you ever noticed how easy it is, when you’re building a life with someone, to start losing track of who you are as an individual? Between work, family, and all the things you share, it gets tough to find time for your own interests and passions. Over time, those boundaries that made you feel like your own person can start to blur, and it’s almost like you forget what used to make you feel alive.
But here’s something to really pay attention to: that sense of individuality—the feeling that you’re your own person—is one of the biggest sparks for desire. Attraction often grows in that space between you and your partner, where you recognize that, yes, you know them so well, but there’s still a part of them that’s mysterious and new.
When you keep your own identity alive—when you chase after your interests, hang out with your friends, or get lost in a passion project—you’re actually bringing fresh energy and excitement right back into your relationship.
Let me share a quick story. There was a man who, after years of marriage, realized he’d stopped doing the things that made him feel truly alive. So much of his focus was on being a partner and a parent, he lost touch with his own dreams and ambitions. And that spark, that attraction to his partner, started to fade. It wasn’t until he began to reclaim his sense of self—picking up old hobbies, setting aside time for friends, and drawing healthy boundaries—that he felt that old spark return.
And he’s not alone. So many people think the secret to a happy relationship is to blend your lives together completely—to share everything, do everything as a pair. But honestly, desire doesn’t thrive in that kind of closeness. It grows when there’s a little space, a little longing and curiosity left between you.
One woman put it beautifully. She said she felt most attracted to her partner when she saw him lost in something he loved—playing music, deep in a project, or laughing with friends. In those moments, he seemed both familiar and excitingly new. That little bit of distance, that sense of watching him from the outside, made her want to reach out and connect.
So, keeping your individuality isn’t about pulling away or building walls. It’s about respecting your own needs and dreams, and letting your partner do the same. It’s about remembering that every strong relationship is built on two whole people, each with their own lives and passions.
When you make space for your individuality, you actually bring more energy and excitement to your relationship. You don’t just see each other as roommates or co-parents, but as lovers—people with their own desires, dreams, and a bit of mystery. That’s what keeps longing alive, even in the middle of everyday life.
So here’s the key takeaway: desire grows in that space between you and your partner, in the recognition that they’re both familiar and mysterious. By holding on to your individuality—by pursuing what lights you up—you help keep that spark alive, even as you build a life together.
